observation.visible_scene: A dance studio with white walls, a full-length mirror wall on the right, ceiling track lighting, a wall-mounted AC unit, and a light curtain. A woman with a dark ponytail (blue hair tie), a sleeveless blue dress, and black thigh-high boots stands with her back to the camera, facing the mirror; her front-facing image in the mirror is her reflection, not a second person. The camera framing and background stay fixed across all frames.
visible_changes: At t=0.000 the dancer's right arm is extended out to the side, roughly horizontal with a flat hand, while the left arm is bent at her hip; the mirror reflection shows the matching pose.
From t=0.040 to t=0.120 the extended right arm holds its outward position with only small hand/forearm adjustments.
From t=0.160 to t=0.280 the right arm bends and draws inward toward the chest, and the reflection's arms move from a one-arm-out pose to both arms crossing in front of the torso.
From t=0.320 to t0.640 both hands rise in front of the upper chest and face, palms turned toward each other in a framing gesture; the reflection mirrors this.

From t=0.680 to t=1.160 the hands lower to the neck/collarbone and chin area, palms flat near the throat and jaw, holding a face-framing pose; the reflected face appears to smile during this interval.
From t=1.200 to t=1.440 the hands begin to separate and drop away from the face/neck.
From t=1.480 to t=1.600 both arms fall open and down toward the sides of the body.
Throughout the later half (roughly t=0.680 onward) the dancer's knees flex and hips shift into a slight bent-knee stance, and the skirt sways accordingly; the reflection shows the same leg bend.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0.000 and after t=1.600 is not shown, so the gesture sequence's start, end, and musical context are unknown.
Whether the knee bend is a deliberate pose or a weight shift is not determinable from the segment alone.
uncertain_details: The exact intended meaning of the hand gestures (framing the face, touching the neck) is interpretive; only the hand/arm positions are directly visible.
Minor hand-position differences between consecutive frames are small and may reflect continuous motion rather than distinct poses.
